cards.prompt: Create a NumPy array from the list [10, 20, 30, 40, 50].
cards.why: np.array() converts a Python list into a NumPy array, unlocking vectorized operations.
cards.whenToUse: Whenever you need fast, element-wise math on numeric data.
cards.commonMistake: Expecting a plain Python list to support element-wise arithmetic like arr * 2 — it doesn't.

cards.prompt: Multiply every element of arr by 2.
cards.why: Arithmetic on a NumPy array applies element-wise, with no explicit loop needed.
cards.whenToUse: Any per-element transformation on numeric data.
cards.commonMistake: Writing a Python for-loop to multiply each element — vectorized ops are faster and more idiomatic.

cards.prompt: Select only the elements of arr greater than 25.
cards.why: arr > 25 produces a boolean array used to filter arr itself, the same pattern used for pandas boolean indexing.
cards.whenToUse: Filtering numeric data by a condition.
cards.commonMistake: Trying arr.filter(...) — NumPy arrays don't have a filter() method; boolean masking is the idiom.

cards.prompt: Average of all elements in arr.
cards.why: mean() is a built-in reduction method on any NumPy array.
cards.whenToUse: Summarizing a whole array with a single statistic.
cards.commonMistake: Using sum(arr) / len(arr) manually when .mean() does the same thing directly.

cards.prompt: Create a range of 6 numbers and reshape it into a 2x3 matrix.
cards.why: reshape() rearranges the same data into a new shape, as long as the total element count matches.
cards.whenToUse: Converting a flat sequence into a 2D (or higher) matrix layout.
cards.commonMistake: Requesting a shape whose dimensions don't multiply to the original element count, which raises a ValueError.

cards.prompt: Create an array of 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 using a range-like function instead of listing each number.
cards.why: arange(start, stop, step) generates evenly spaced values, stopping before the stop value.
cards.whenToUse: Generating a sequence with a known start, stop, and step size.
cards.commonMistake: Expecting the stop value itself to be included — arange's stop bound is exclusive, like Python's range().

cards.prompt: Create 5 evenly spaced numbers from 0 to 1, inclusive of both ends.
cards.why: linspace(start, stop, num) includes both endpoints by default, unlike arange's exclusive stop.
cards.whenToUse: You know how many points you want, not the step size.
cards.commonMistake: Using arange when you actually care about the count of points rather than the step size.

cards.prompt: Standard deviation of all elements in arr.
cards.why: std() is a built-in reduction, same family as mean()/sum().
cards.commonMistake: Manually computing variance and forgetting to square-root it, when .std() does both steps.

cards.prompt: Replace every element of arr that's 25 or under with 0, keeping the rest unchanged.
cards.why: where(condition, if_true, if_false) picks element-wise between two values based on a boolean condition.
cards.whenToUse: Conditionally replacing values without a Python loop.
cards.commonMistake: Using boolean masking (arr[arr>25]) when you need to keep the original shape with replaced values, not a shorter filtered array.

cards.prompt: Index of the largest element in arr.
cards.why: argmax() returns the position of the maximum value, not the value itself.
cards.whenToUse: Finding where a peak occurs, not just what the peak value is.
cards.commonMistake: Calling .max() and expecting a position back instead of the value.

cards.why: cumsum() returns an array the same length as the input, where each element is the sum of all elements up to that point.
cards.whenToUse: Running totals, e.g. cumulative revenue over time.
cards.commonMistake: Confusing cumsum() (returns an array) with sum() (returns a single number).

cards.prompt: Sort arr from largest to smallest.
cards.why: np.sort() always sorts ascending; reversing the sorted result with [::-1] gives descending order.
cards.whenToUse: Ranking numeric data from highest to lowest.
cards.commonMistake: Expecting a descending= keyword argument on np.sort() — it doesn't have one.

cards.prompt: Reshape a range of 6 numbers into a 2x3 matrix, then sum each column (not each row).
cards.why: axis=0 sums down columns; axis=1 would sum across rows instead.
cards.whenToUse: Aggregating a 2D array along one specific dimension.
cards.commonMistake: Mixing up axis=0 (columns) and axis=1 (rows) — a very common source of subtle bugs.

cards.prompt: Convert arr's dtype to float. Fill in the blank.
cards.why: astype() converts an array's dtype, returning a new array without modifying the original.
cards.whenToUse: You need floating-point division/precision instead of the array's current dtype.
cards.commonMistake: Assuming arithmetic automatically upcasts dtype in place — astype() returns a new array; it doesn't mutate arr.

cards.prompt: Which correctly computes the element-wise squares of arr?
cards.why: ** raises each element to a power directly; multiplying by 2 doubles instead of squaring.
cards.whenToUse: Any element-wise power operation on numeric data.
cards.commonMistake: Confusing multiplying by 2 (arr * 2) with squaring (arr ** 2) — very different operations that both 'look like' scaling.
